variables.title: Variables
variables.code:
set name "Fish User"
set -l local_var "local"
set -g global_var "global"
variables.notes: Fish does not use `=` for assignment, it uses the `set` command.

data_types.title: Data Types
data_types.notes: Fish uses lists (arrays) natively; variables are fundamentally lists of strings.

operators.title: Operators
operators.notes: Fish uses the `math` command instead of expr or `(())`.

conditionals.title: Conditionals
conditionals.code:
if test $a -gt $b
  echo "Greater"
else if test $a -eq $b
  echo "Equal"
else
  echo "Less"
end

while_loop.title: While Loop
while_loop.code:
while test $i -lt 5
  echo $i
  set i (math $i + 1)
end

functions.title: Functions
functions.code:
function greet
  set name $argv[1]
  echo "Hello $name"
end
functions.notes: Uses `$argv` instead of `$1` (though `$1` may work). No `{}`.

maps.title: Maps
maps.code:
# Simulating with parallel lists
set keys key1 key2
set vals val1 val2

error_handling.title: Error Handling
error_handling.notes: Uses `and`/`or` instead of `&&`/`||` in older versions (though newer fish supports them).

comments.title: Comments & Documentation
comments.code:
# Single-line comment in Hy

"""
Multi-line documentation block.
Provides docstrings for functions and modules.
"""

def add(a, b):
    """Return sum of a and b."""
    return a + b
comments.notes: Hy uses # for line comments and triple quotes for multi-line documentation strings.

numbers.title: Numbers & Numerics
numbers.notes: Hy supports arbitrary-precision or native integers, IEEE floats, and numeric literal prefixes (0x, 0b).

booleans.title: Booleans & Conditions
booleans.code:
is_active = True
has_failed = False

if is_active and not has_failed:
    print("Active")
booleans.notes: Hy represents boolean values with logical and, or, and not operators.

type_casting.title: Type Casting & Conversion
type_casting.code:
num_str = "42"
n = int(num_str)
f = float(n)
s = str(f)
type_casting.notes: Hy uses explicit conversion functions or operators to transform types between primitives.

strings.title: Strings & Escapes
strings.code:
s1 = "Double-quoted string"
s2 = 'Single-quoted string'
raw = r"C:\new_folder\raw.txt"
multi = """Line 1
Line 2"""
strings.notes: Hy supports single, double, and raw string literals that ignore escape characters.

string_formatting.title: String Formatting
string_formatting.code:
name = "Alice"
score = 95
msg = f"User {name} scored {score:.1f}"
print(msg)
string_formatting.notes: Hy uses f-string interpolation or format specifiers for embedded expression formatting.

pattern_matching.title: Pattern Matching
pattern_matching.code:
match val:
    case 1:
        print("One")
    case 2 | 3:
        print("Two or Three")
    case _:
        print("Default")
pattern_matching.notes: Hy provides structural pattern matching with match/case or case-of expressions.

range.title: Ranges & Slices
range.code:
r = range(1, 10, 2)
sub = nums[1:5]
rev = nums[::-1]
range.notes: Hy provides built-in range generation and slicing syntax with interval boundaries.

iterators.title: Iterators & Generators
iterators.notes: Hy uses generator functions or iterators with the yield keyword for lazy element production.

oop_classes.title: Classes & OOP
oop_classes.notes: Hy supports object-oriented paradigms with methods, constructors, and encapsulation.

lists.title: Lists & Dynamic Arrays
lists.notes: Hy provides mutable dynamic lists/sequences with append, insert, and indexing operations.

tuples.title: Tuples & Records
tuples.notes: Hy provides immutable ordered tuples supporting unpack destructuring.

sets.title: Sets & Collections
sets.notes: Hy provides unique element set collections with membership tests and mathematical set operations.

modules_import.title: Modules & Imports
modules_import.code:
import math
from math import sqrt, pi
import os.path as path
modules_import.notes: Hy manages code organization via modules and selective import statements.
